# Fixes — Remedies for Periodic RA Spikes (EQ6 Family)

**Dimension:** documented remedies, their mechanism, which generation they apply to, and
outcome. Emphasis on what remains after bearings and belts have been replaced. Sources:
[citations.md](../citations.md).

## Fixes table

| # | Fix | Mechanism | Generation | Evidence | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Replace aftermarket worm bearings with standard 608s** | Defective / non-standard worm-shaft bearing | Legacy EQ6 (same worm) | [15] | **133 s spike gone; 0.4" RMS** |
| 2 | Re-centre and re-tension belt; remove worm-gear slop on shaft | Belt misalignment, axial/radial worm play | Exos2-GT | [16] | ~134 s spike "completely gone" (with cable and polar-alignment changes; not isolated) |
| 3 | Back off RA worm mesh | Over-tight mesh → sticking | Legacy EQ6 + belt kit | [28] | Spikes gone; slight tone change while slewing was the tell |
| 4 | Loosen worm housing, belt, RA axis lock nut | Binding | EQ6-R | [24] | Reported improvement; confounded by wrong focal length |
| 5 | Belt slack 4–5 mm (Sky-Watcher) / deflection ≤3–4 mm mid-span (owner) | Over-tight belt makes motor pulley wobble | EQ6-R Pro | [21] / [29] | Not reported / Dec backlash 3000 → 900 ms |
| 6 | Replace deformed motor pulley; grub screw onto shaft flat | Eccentric pulley (120 s line) | EQ6-R Pro / NEQ6 kit | [21] / [6] | Not reported |
| 7 | GT2 15/60 pulleys in place of stock T2.5 12/48 | Belt tooth-mesh error (10 s line) | EQ6-R | [26][27] | 10 s peak removed |
| 8 | Worm end-float nut "just over finger tight"; lock nut back off 1/10 turn | Over-preload damages the small end-float bearing / blocks rotation in cold | EQ6-R Pro / legacy EQ6 | [25] / [4] | Qualitative |
| 9 | Worm mesh in steps of 1/8 turn or less, run 360° to check binding | Even mesh, no tight spots | NEQ6 | [6] | Qualitative |
| 10 | Replace RA motor | Motor fault | EQ6-R Pro | [18] | **Failed** (133 s case) |
| 11 | Firmware update | Controller | EQ6R Pro | [17] | **Failed** ("No change") |
| 12 | Regrease / clean | Grit | Legacy EQ6 | [28]; [19] | Random 2" spikes gone [28]; Waddington ranks grit "less likely" [19] |
| 13 | PEC / PPEC | Cancels worm-synchronous error only | All | [30]; [38] | 0.6–0.9" total [30]; non-worm-synchronous vibration "cannot be corrected by PEC" [38] |

## What applies to a mount already rebuilt with new bearings and belts

1. **The bearings themselves are a candidate, not a closed question.** In the one resolved
   EQ6-family 133 s case, the spike was *caused* by replacement ("upgraded") worm bearings
   and fixed by returning to original 608s [15]. Replacement 608s are not all equivalent:
   EQ6-R kits list 608 2Z/C3 [7] or 608-2RSH [8]; Astrobloke reported being told "the
   correct replacement are the metal shielded 608 2z", with another user reporting binding
   from the 2RS type [29]; ceramic hybrid kits do not publish geometry [13], and at least one
   "608" hybrid has 4 balls instead of 7 [14].
2. **Installation damage is documented.** Tightening worm end float until it binds can
   knock "the small end float bearing … slightly out of shape" [25].
3. **Belt tension is an active variable even with new belts.** Sky-Watcher's stated minimum
   is 4–5 mm slack [21]; an owner's check is ≤3–4 mm deflection [29] — these two figures are
   measured differently (slack vs mid-span deflection) and are not directly comparable. An
   over-tight belt is linked to motor-pulley wobble [21], which appears at ~120 s, not 136 s
   [20][22].
4. **Motor and firmware replacement have failed in matching cases** [17][18].
5. **Full bearing replacement is not required for most gains**, per one owner; Sky-Watcher axes are often delivered over-torqued [31]. Adjustment, not new parts, gave most of the benefit in that account.

## Risks

- Over-tight worm mesh: sticking spikes [28]; seizure in cold [4]; binding [24].
- Over-tight end-float nut: bearing deformation [25]; blocked rotation in cold [4].
- Over-tight belt: friction [4]; pulley wobble [21].
- Bearing type substitution: 608 2RS vs 2Z binding report (second-hand) [29].

## Gaps and limitations

- No torque or tension specification is published in the Sky-Watcher manual [1].
- Fix 1 is a single case on a legacy EQ6; its ceramic bearing geometry is unknown [15][13].
- Fix 2 coincided with a re-plugged RA serial cable and redone polar alignment [16]; the cause is not isolated.
- No fetched source reports a fix on an EQ6-R Pro for a 130–140 s spike.
